title: A Hierarchical Statistical Framework for Evaluating Agent Reliability
abstract: arXiv:2611.19614v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Agents operating in complex scenarios often face uncertainty due to incomplete information about the environment they operate in, ambiguous user queries, complex business rules and the inherently stochastic dynamics of the governing policy. Several new benchmarks have been proposed to evaluate LLM-based agents on complex tasks in multi-tool environments, including settings with policy constraints and varying levels of intent ambiguity. These conditions make it important to evaluate agentic systems systematically and quantify their performance under different conditions to assess their reliability in production. This need is evident in the recently introduced Thinkingbox benchmark, where even the strongest models struggle to perform consistently across diverse business scenarios. translated_title: 评估智能体可靠性的分层统计框架
translated_abstract: 在复杂场景中运行的智能体常常面临不确定性，这源于对其运行环境的信息不完整、用户查询的模糊性、复杂的业务规则以及控制策略本身固有的随机动态特性。目前已有多个新基准被提出，用于在多工具环境中评估基于大语言模型（LLM）的智能体在复杂任务上的表现，其中包括带有策略约束和不同意图模糊程度的设置。这些条件使得对智能体系统进行系统性评估、并量化其在不同条件下的性能以评估其生产可靠性变得至关重要。这一需求在最近推出的 Thinkingbox 基准中尤为明显——即使是性能最强的模型，也难以在多样化的业务场景中保持一致的表现。本文提出了一个用于评估智能体系统不确定性与可靠性的统计框架。我们定义了一个由场景、实例和采样构成的层次结构。
tldr: 本文提出了一个分层统计框架，通过定义场景、实例和采样的层次结构，系统性地量化智能体系统在不同条件下的不确定性与可靠性。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a hierarchical statistical framework that defines a hierarchy of scenarios, instances, and samples to systematically quantify the uncertainty and reliability of agentic systems under varying conditions.
